title: Will France declare a state of emergency before Nov 1, 2026?
rules: If the French government declares a state of emergency (état d'urgence) after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Only reporting from Bloomberg News, Reuters, the Associated Press, or Le Monde qualifies. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify unless the new publication explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of its publication date. Republishing of content from other sources qualifies only if hosted on the outlet’s official platform with that outlet identified as publisher.

A state of emergency (état d'urgence) is one declared by decree of the President of France in the Council of Ministers under Law No. 55-385 of April 3, 1955, for all or part of French territory, including overseas territories. It counts when the decree is adopted, not when it is merely announced, requested or under consideration.

Curfews, protest bans and other measures taken by prefects or mayors, Article 16 or state-of-siege powers, a state of health emergency (état d'urgence sanitaire), and natural-disaster declarations do not count.

blind.reasoning: France is in its worst unrest in years after the October 17-18 riots, and PM Lecornu has said he could declare a state of emergency 'if needed.' However, the government has openly said it prefers curfews, which don't count. The interior minister reportedly ruled out an emergency 'for now', and declaring one against political protests before the 2027 election is costly. With only about 11 days left, YES needs the unrest to keep escalating or curfews to visibly fail, as happened in 2005.
blind.falsifier: A decree under the 1955 law adopted in the Council of Ministers before Nov 1, 2026 and reported by Reuters, AP, Bloomberg or Le Monde. On the NO side, a clear calming of the riots under curfews in the next week would confirm this forecast.

final.reasoning: I'm moving from 0.24 to 0.21 because the market may reflect news after October 20 that I couldn't see. A one-point edge over the 0.20 ask is too thin to justify buying YES, so I'm passing.
